verified_findings.claim: The first local elections were held in two stages: city/eup/myeon councils on 1952-04-25 and provincial councils on 1952-05-10.
verified_findings.note: The NEC museum reports turnout of 80.2% city, 88.4% eup, 93.1% myeon, and 81.2% provincial.

verified_findings.claim: The 1952-05-10 provincial election created a large pool of independently identifiable local political actors; contemporary NIHK material preserves constituency-level names and votes for Busan/Gyeongnam and a separate Daegu/Gyeongbuk report.
verified_findings.note: Names are treated as local-politician candidates, not assumed to be national politicians.

verified_findings.claim: The executive constitutional program was already formalized before the May 1952 crisis: the 1951 government proposal combined direct presidential election and bicameralism, was rejected on 1952-01-18, and the government renewed its proposal in May.

Immediately before martial law, Rhee appointed Yi Pom-sok Interior Minister, Hong Pom-hui vice minister and Yun U-gyeong police chief; FRUS records the appointments and the subsequent martial-law declaration.
verified_findings.attribution_rule: Appointment and institutional command position do not by themselves prove authorship of each later arrest.

verified_findings.claim: The constitutional crisis involved distinct institutional actors rather than a president-only event: Cabinet, Interior Ministry, police, martial-law command, National Assembly factions, local representatives and foreign diplomatic observers all appear in separate records.

The 1952-07-04 amendment passed with 163 votes among 166 present and was promulgated 1952-07-07; its core effects included direct presidential election, bicameral legislature and a National Assembly no-confidence mechanism.
The first direct presidential election occurred 1952-08-05. Official archival election data report Rhee 5,238,769 votes, Cho Bong-am 797,504, Yi Si-yeong 764,715 and Sin Heung-u 219,696.

The vice-presidential contest was a separate multi-actor election. NIHK chronology reports Ham Tae-yeong 2,943,813, Yi Pom-sok 1,815,692, Cho Byeong-ok 575,260, Yi Gap-seong 500,927, Yi Yun-yeong 458,583, Jeon Jin-han 302,471, Baek Seong-uk 181,388 and Jeong Gi-won 164,907.

The June 25 assassination attempt should be modeled separately from the later government allegation of a political conspiracy. Contemporary reporting establishes Yu Si-tae's attempted shooting and immediate arrest; a July 3 Interior Minister statement names alleged associates, while the August court process supplies a later judicial layer.
verified_findings.attribution_rule: Government allegation is not silently converted into judicially established fact.

verified_findings.claim: The International Club case requires a correction layer: a later August 15 contemporary report says all 30 related persons received non-prosecution dispositions, despite earlier arrests/investigation.
verified_findings.note: Preserve arrest/investigation and prosecutorial disposition as different event states.

adversarial_checks: Tested a president-only narrative of the 1952 crisis against Cabinet, Interior, martial-law, Assembly and FRUS records; retained multi-actor attribution.
Tested whether Yi Pom-sok's ministerial appointment proves each arrest order; it does not, so HD-RHEE-006 remains NARROWED.
Tested whether the 1952 amendment was a single spontaneous July compromise; official cabinet records show an executive proposal chain from 1951.

Tested the common 'excerpt compromise' shorthand against National Archives' own interpretive exhibit, which argues government preferences dominated; preserved interpretation as interpretation rather than settled fact.
Tested whether local elections can be treated as a footnote to national constitutional conflict; official election records show a distinct institutional event and a large local-politician corpus.
Tested whether all 1952 provincial-election winners should immediately enter national politician registry; held most at DISCOVERED pending identity/office-depth verification.
Tested government conspiracy allegations in the assassination attempt against later judicial layers; kept allegation, defendant status and judgment as separate evidence states.
Tested International Club arrests against later prosecutorial outcome; contemporary report records non-prosecution for all 30.
Tested regular political opposition to Rhee against criminal-conspiracy attribution; no automatic equivalence is allowed.
Tested 1952 presidential and vice-presidential results across National Archives/NEC/NIHK public-institution families; dates and main presidential totals converge.
Tested martial-law date wording across midnight boundary; retained 24/25 May source convention instead of forcing false precision.
Tested temporary Assembly chairmanship as mere biography; it is retained as a procedural event showing legislative institutional continuity during crisis.

Next target remains martial-law command arrest lists/orders plus National Assembly/헌병 records.
